title: Contractor selection, quotes and approvals
audience: Home-based property managers who select contractors and obtain quotes for owners
learningOutcomes: Select contractors by licence position, scope fit and evidence of competence, without assuming a licence.
Obtain comparable written quotes against the same scope.
Route quotes through the owner's approval before any work is booked.

instruction.heading: Check the licence position before selection
instruction.body: A contractor is selected for the work, not for their name. For each trade, check the licence position for the state, and ask the contractor to show their licence or registration number and the class it covers. Do not record a licence as held because the contractor says so. In New South Wales, a contractor licence is needed for residential building or trade work, fencing included, where the value of the work exceeds $5,000 with GST included (page last updated 23 June 2026). Record what was checked, when, and by whom.

instruction.heading: Compare quotes on the same scope
instruction.body: Give each contractor the same written scope, the same access details and the same exclusions, and ask for a written quote against it. Quotes that cover different scopes cannot be compared, and a low quote that leaves out a task is not a saving. Compare the exclusions as carefully as the price. Route each quote to the owner for approval, and book work only after written approval is received. Variations are approved in writing before they are performed.

procedure: Confirm the licence position for each trade in the state, and check the contractor's licence or registration details.
Record what was checked, when, and by whom.
Give each contractor the same scope, access details and exclusions in writing.
Compare quotes line by line, including exclusions.
Send the chosen quote to the owner for written approval.
Book the work only after approval, and record each variation's approval.

workedExamples.situation: Three quotes arrive for a fence repair. The lowest excludes removal of the old posts, which the others include.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the lowest quote the best choice?
workedExamples.reasoning: Not on price alone. The lowest quote excludes a task the others include, so the quotes are not for the same scope. Ask the lowest contractor to quote the removal or state the exclusion clearly, and send the comparison to the owner for approval. Check the licence position for the fence work in the state before booking.

commonErrors.error: Recording a licence as held without checking.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the licence or registration and the class it covers, and record the check.

commonErrors.error: Choosing the lowest quote without comparing exclusions.
commonErrors.prevention: Compare each quote against the same scope and exclusions.
Route the quote to the owner and book only after written approval.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Fence work: New South Wales requires a contractor licence for fencing when the work value exceeds $5,000 with GST included (page last updated 23 June 2026). The QBCC's general threshold for building work is $3,300 (no page date shown). Confirm the position before booking.
Gas fitting, plumbing and drainage work in Queensland needs a licence whatever its value, according to the QBCC page (no page date shown). Check the state's licence list before booking.
Completing this lesson does not give a contractor licence or authority to select contractors on the owner's behalf without approval.

qualityStandard: The licence position is checked and recorded for each trade before booking.
Quotes are compared on the same written scope and exclusions.
No work is booked without written owner approval.
documentationEvidence: Contractor licence check record with date and checker
Quote comparison sheet with scope and exclusions
Written owner approval for the chosen quote
summary: Check the licence position and the contractor's class before booking.
Compare quotes on the same scope, including the exclusions.
Book only after the owner's written approval.

knowledgeChecks.question: The lowest quote for a repair excludes a task the others include. What should happen?
options: Book the lowest quote, since the saving is good for the owner and the whole portfolio today
Ignore the exclusion, since the owner only wants the lowest price on the sheet for the whole job
Split the difference between the quotes, so the price sits in the middle of the two of them
Compare on the same scope, ask for the excluded task to be quoted, and send the comparison for approval

knowledgeChecks.question: A contractor says they hold the licence. What should the manager do?
options: Check the licence or registration and the class it covers, and record the check
Record the licence as held without checking the class of it at all
Book the contractor without checking, since they seem to be fine for the job
Ask the owner to check the licence before the job is booked in at all today

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say work is booked?
options: As soon as the lowest quote arrives
Before the owner sees the quotes
Only after written approval from the owner is received
